title: Written Norm Redlines
summary: Avoid high-visibility errors in formal Brazilian Portuguese involving agreement, regency, pronouns, crase, and punctuation.

sections.heading: Agreement that readers notice
sections.body: Formal writing requires consistent subject-verb and noun-adjective agreement. Collective and postposed subjects can be tricky, but clarity usually favors standard agreement.

examples.en: Documents are missing from the file.

examples.note: singular with maioria as head noun

sections.heading: Regency and crase redlines
sections.body: Mistakes with required prepositions and crase are highly visible in edited writing. Check both the word before and the feminine article after.

examples.en: I refer to the proposal sent yesterday.

examples.note: no crase before plural without as

sections.heading: Pronouns and punctuation
sections.body: Formal writing avoids many spoken pronoun patterns and uses punctuation to show sentence structure, not spoken pauses alone.

examples.en: I informed him about the change.
I did not find him at the meeting.

examples.pt: Embora o prazo seja curto, a equipe conseguirá concluir o trabalho.
examples.en: Although the deadline is short, the team will be able to finish the work.

keyPoints: Formal redlines include agreement, regency, crase, pronoun choice, and punctuation.
Spoken patterns may be natural but still inappropriate in edited writing.
Crase requires both preposition a and feminine article/pronoun.
Revise formal texts specifically for these high-visibility issues.

commonMistakes.note: Plural subject after the verb still triggers plural agreement.
Referir-se a + a proposta = à proposta.

commonMistakes.wrong: Embora o prazo é curto, vamos entregar.
commonMistakes.right: Embora o prazo seja curto, vamos entregar.
